<oralStatements><speech endTime="2026-10-06T13:43:58.144" startTime="2026-10-06T13:42:52.925" xml:lang="sk-t-en-mtec"><from xml:lang="sk-t-en-mtec" xml:space="preserve"><person refersTo="epdata:person/197770">Martin Hojsík</person> (<organization refersTo="epdata:org/7035">Renew</organization>).</from></speech></oralStatements>

Marcin Sypniewski (ESN), reaction to a blue card.

I agree that we need to talk about real things. For me, such a real thing is the cost. If we only manipulate and change small things, and we do not reach for what really burdens the pocket of an ordinary European citizen – that is, that he pays more and more for electricity, that the costs of all procedures are piling up and increasing, that we have to pay more and more for heating, for transport – then we will not solve any problem. It is not a solution to subtract everything from the market, because it will end with what has always been.

<oralStatements><speech endTime="2026-10-06T13:11:19.284" startTime="2026-10-06T13:09:46.75" xml:lang="cs-t-en-mtec"><from xml:lang="cs-t-en-mtec" xml:space="preserve"><person refersTo="epdata:person/256853">Klara Dostalova</person>, <role refersTo="">on behalf of the Group <organization refersTo="epdata:org/7150">PfE</organization></role>.</from></speech></oralStatements>

<oralStatements><speech endTime="2026-10-06T13:01:37.024" startTime="2026-10-06T12:57:43.15" xml:lang="en"><from xml:lang="en" xml:space="preserve"><person refersTo="epdata:person/275105">Thomas Byrne</person>, <role refersTo="">President-in-Office of the Council</role>.</from></speech></oralStatements>

<oralStatements><speech endTime="2026-10-06T14:53:26.067" startTime="2026-10-06T14:52:20.034" xml:lang="el-t-en-mtec"><from xml:lang="el-t-en-mtec" xml:space="preserve"><person refersTo="epdata:person/197699">Έλενα Κουντουρά</person> (<organization refersTo="epdata:org/7036">The Left</organization>).</from></speech></oralStatements>

<writtenStatements><speech xml:lang="ro-t-en-mtec"><from xml:lang="ro-t-en-mtec" xml:space="preserve"><person refersTo="epdata:person/257098">Gabriela Firea</person> (<organization refersTo="epdata:org/7038">S&D</organization>), <process refersTo="">in writing</process></from></speech></writtenStatements>

Marcin Sypniewski (ESN), answer to a blue card question.

I think I'm happy. However, like every resident of the European Union, I would like the costs of maintaining a house to be much lower. It is abnormal that the costs we spend on housing sometimes run out of the entire family budget, and these costs keep increasing. It is enough to see what happens to the heating, what happens to the electricity, what also happens to the transport.

How difficult it is for a person who lives outside big cities to get to the doctor, to school, to work, to university. All this, however, causes that it reaches more and more into the pockets of an ordinary man.

Idoia Mendia (S&D), blue card question.

Thanks to the efforts of the Social Democrats, we have managed to have in this legislature a commissioner, a commission, a plan and now an Affordable Housing Law, to which the PP has already expressed its opposite position. Do you not think that Europe should plan affordable housing with the whole life cycle in mind, young and old, and above all ban vulture funds, ensure that the elderly can choose where they want to continue living, that there are no more Maricármenes that the Popular Party leaves homeless at the end of their lives?

<oralStatements><speech endTime="2026-10-06T14:34:29.433" startTime="2026-10-06T14:33:21.322" xml:lang="de-t-en-mtec"><from xml:lang="de-t-en-mtec" xml:space="preserve"><person refersTo="epdata:person/38511">Georg Mayer</person> (<organization refersTo="epdata:org/7150">PfE</organization>).</from></speech></oralStatements>

<oralStatements><speech endTime="2026-10-06T13:40:34.851" startTime="2026-10-06T13:39:20.9" xml:lang="es-t-en-mtec"><from xml:lang="es-t-en-mtec" xml:space="preserve"><person refersTo="epdata:person/247735">Laura Ballarín Cereza</person> (<organization refersTo="epdata:org/7038">S&D</organization>).</from></speech></oralStatements>

Lukas Sieper (Renew), Reaction according to the procedure of the "blue card".

Mr. Colleague – I'm changing to German now – I even agree with you that we have a crisis. I agree with you that the cost is too high. I agree with you that the burden on people is too high. And you may be surprised, but the authors of this legislative process agree with you. That's why I wonder why you're wasting your time here attacking these people personally, subordinating them to double standards, subordinating them to living a privileged life of their own while actually advocating for the people. So why, instead of attacking the people here, can you not rather deal with the arguments in the matter?

<oralStatements><speech endTime="2026-10-06T15:00:37.522" startTime="2026-10-06T15:00:32.255" xml:lang="fr-t-en-mtec"><from xml:lang="fr-t-en-mtec"><person refersTo="epdata:person/30482">Le Président</person>.</from></speech></oralStatements>

<oralStatements><speech endTime="2026-10-06T14:44:25.144" startTime="2026-10-06T14:43:18.498" xml:lang="sv-t-en-mtec"><from xml:lang="sv-t-en-mtec" xml:space="preserve"><person refersTo="epdata:person/38542">Johan Danielsson</person> (<organization refersTo="epdata:org/7038">S&D</organization>).</from></speech></oralStatements>

Marcin Sypniewski (ESN).

Mr President, thank you very much. I really admire the insolence of the political caste. You promise cheap housing, but first you bill the citizens, and then you announce that you are coming to their aid. What is behind the promise of cheap housing? With the other hand, you add to people the costs of construction, heating, electricity and repairs. To build a house, you have to go through more and more difficult procedures. Someone has to pay for it – with time and money. And this bill gets a family who wanted their own four walls.

Added to this is the blinding of green politics. After all, the ETS burdens the production of cement, energy and steel. The cost of emission allowances doesn't disappear just because you say it's about saving the climate. And the nail in the coffin will be ETS 2, which will further increase costs.

The citizen is only really interested in you when you can reach into his pocket. You talk about saving the planet from a comfortable home, sipping coffee from the other end of the world, and an ordinary man has to refuel, get to work and warm the apartment.

(The speaker agreed to the blue card question)

Kathleen Funchion (The Left).

Mr President, I welcome this debate on the Housing Act. While the Act is limited, there are recommendations that we should implement, particularly in areas such as the Gaeltacht - with a large number of holiday homes and short-term rentals. We all know that there is more to be done to ensure a bright future for our Gaeltachts - now is time to act. Housing is important for our society and, at present, too expensive for the next generation. In Ireland, the housing crisis has been ongoing for more than a decade. And what is the government doing? Giving tax relief to developers who are already making big profits. It is time to choose a different direction. It's time to get this pain right.

api:xmlFragment.en:
Lukas Sieper (NI), Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“.

Madam President, In line with our Rules of Procedure, I would also like to be able to respond to my colleague's reply.

Dear colleague, thank you for accepting the blue card.

If I understood you correctly, you said that when your party wins the next election, you will not participate as a Member State in the distribution of migrants. So am I understanding you correctly that you are saying that if you win the election you will breach European Union law? And has that not, under the Dublin system, led to all this chaos that we have, that Member States did not follow through with European law? Should we not respect the law?

activity_label.en: The role of the EU in efforts for peace and stability throughout the Middle East after the announced deal between the US and Iran (debate)
Ongoing persecution of Christians in Nigeria, notably the Kawel village massacre

api:xmlFragment.en:
Lukas Sieper (Renew), Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“.

Madam President, can I still catch-the-eye or one of them? Both, okay.

Thank you, dear colleague, for accepting the blue card. I'm with you in your anger. I just want to state that up front.

I listened to your speech very thoroughly, so I have one simple question: for you, is there a difference between a Muslim and an Islamist?

Thank you.
